card.situation:
SWFPAC (Dept. of the Navy) solicits a firm-fixed-price professional services contract to migrate a legacy Microsoft Access 2003 warehouse/inventory database to the Navy's Microsoft 365 "Flank Speed" platform using SharePoint Online, Power Apps, and Power Automate, with UAT support and a Migration Guide, delivered 100% remotely within 180 calendar days.
This notice reached the owner because Sooner Systems' NAICS 541512 matches, the firm holds SDVOSB status, and one past-performance record references a Microsoft 365 migration.
reasons_for: CMMC Level 2 self-assessed exceeds the contract's CMMC Level 1 (Self) threshold, removing a common DoN compliance barrier [e4ca493c-4379a941-p22-72f61d3e].
The 100% remote place of performance aligns perfectly with the firm's Norman, OK facility and existing 24x7 NOC delivery model [e4ca493c-4379a941-p7-ff39d287].
NAICS 541512 matches the solicitation and the firm's SDVOSB status remains valid; the unrestricted set-aside does not disqualify the firm [e4ca493c-4379a941-p20-dec1759d].
reasons_against: No Microsoft certifications of any kind are listed in the firm profile, making it impossible to submit the required certification documentation with the quote — a hard submission requirement [e4ca493c-259937fc-p6-7b7c35a5].

The firm has no stated Power Apps, Power Automate, SharePoint Online architecture, or Access 2003 migration capability; 23 of 37 requirements are gaps directly tied to these missing technical competencies [e4ca493c-259937fc-p5-4a872785].

Only one past-performance record touches M365 migration (Oklahoma National Guard) and it does not reference Access-to-Power Platform work; the solicitation explicitly requires documented evidence of Access-to-M365/Power Platform migration competency, and the owner's two-PP rule cannot be satisfied [e4ca493c-4379a941-p5-5f3a9177].

key_dates.period_of_performance: 180 calendar days from date of contract award
source_quotes: 5.0 Period of Performance The Period of Performance (PoP) for this effort shall be 180 calendar days from the date of contract award.
All work required under this contract must be completed within 180 calendar days of contract award.
The contractor shall be liable for any nonperformance outside of the required 180 calendar day period of performance.

drafts.capability_statement:
Sooner Systems LLC
Capability Statement — Microsoft 365 Data Migration Project
Notice ID: e4ca493c0b334b3d812882f4bdc2bc4e

Submitted to: Tabbatha Austin, Contracting Officer
Tabbatha.austin@swfpac.navy.mil | Tabbatha.l.austin.civ@us.navy.mil

Sooner Systems LLC is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) headquartered in Norman, Oklahoma, operating under NAICS 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services). We provide information technology professional services to federal government customers including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the FAA, and the Oklahoma National Guard.

Core capabilities relevant to this solicitation:
• Microsoft 365 and Azure administration, including tenant configuration and user migration support
• Systems administration and network engineering
• Cybersecurity services, including CMMC Level 2 self-assessed compliance reflected in SPRS
• 24x7 Network Operations Center (NOC) staffing in Norman, OK, supporting fully remote delivery
• 22 personnel holding active Secret clearances available for sensitive government work

Past Performance: Sooner Systems successfully supported a Microsoft 365 and Active Directory migration for the Oklahoma National Guard (2023–2025, $740,000, NAICS 541512), encompassing systems administration, Exchange migration, and Azure integration.

We are an unrestricted offeror with active SAM registration, NAICS 541512 represented, and current SDVOSB certification. Our Norman, OK facility supports 100% remote performance consistent with the solicitation's place-of-performance requirement.

Sooner Systems LLC | Norman, OK | SDVOSB | NAICS 541512 | CMMC Level 2 (Self)
questions_for_co: Amendment 0001 requires Microsoft certifications in Microsoft 365 and SharePoint Online to be submitted with quotes — will the Government accept a teaming arrangement in which a subcontractor holds the required certifications and provides the certified personnel, or must the prime offeror itself hold all certifications? [e4ca493c-259937fc-p6-7b7c35a5]

SOW paragraph 2.1 requires documented past performance in migrating legacy Microsoft Access systems to Microsoft 365/Power Platform environments — will the Government accept past performance from a proposed subcontractor or key personnel in lieu of, or in addition to, prime contractor past performance? [e4ca493c-4379a941-p5-5f3a9177]

The SOW states the vendor will not be provided access to live data and must evaluate the legacy Access 2003 database structure to propose a target architecture — will the Government provide a sanitized or anonymized schema export, an entity-relationship diagram, or a written description of the existing tables, forms, queries, macros/VBA, and external integrations to support proposal development? [e4ca493c-259937fc-p3-4c75419f]

The solicitation asks offerors to identify any dependency on Dataverse, premium connectors, AI Builder, or other non-standard capabilities — can the Government confirm whether the existing Flank Speed tenant is licensed for Power Apps per-app or per-user plans, and whether any premium connector licenses are already available, so offerors can scope a solution within existing licensing? [e4ca493c-2d7b0065-p21-101ac2c4]

The SOW requires the architecture to support secure archiving of inactive records for a specified timeframe to meet audit requirements — can the Government specify the required retention period (e.g., number of years) and the applicable records-management authority or NARA schedule that governs this data? [e4ca493c-4379a941-p6-3b3eb79a]

The solution must support generation of monthly reporting, but no reporting volume or complexity assumptions are established — can the Government describe the number of distinct report types required, the intended consumers (e.g., command leadership, auditors), and whether reports must be exported to a specific format such as PDF or Excel? [e4ca493c-2d7b0065-p11-99a352de]

reader.scope_summary: SWFPAC requires professional services to migrate a mission-critical Microsoft Access 2003 warehouse and inventory management database to the Navy's Microsoft 365 "Flank Speed" platform, using SharePoint Online as the primary data repository and Microsoft Power Platform (Power Apps and Power Automate) for user interfaces, relational workflows, and automated document generation. The vendor must evaluate the legacy database structure, propose and build an optimized SPO data architecture populated with synthetic test data, facilitate User Acceptance Testing cycles, and deliver a Migration Guide so the Government's internal team can execute the live data transfer. The entire solution must be configured and delivered strictly within the Government's existing Flank Speed cloud environment, 100% remotely, within 180 calendar days of contract award.
quotes: Interested vendors must provide documented evidence of successful past performance and technical competency in designing, deploying, and supporting migrations from legacy Microsoft Access systems to Microsoft 365/Power Platform environments.
Amendment 0001 states that interested vendors must hold Microsoft certifications in Microsoft 365 and SharePoint Online, with certification documentation submitted with quotes.
Certification documentation is required to be submitted with quotes.

The required database architecture and user-facing application must be configured, developed, and delivered strictly within the Government's existing, pre-established Microsoft 365 / SharePoint Online ("Flank Speed") cloud environment.

If a proposed solution depends on premium licensing, premium connectors, Dataverse, AI Builder, or other non-standard capabilities, the offeror shall clearly identify those requirements in the proposal.

CMMC status must be reflected in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) at time of award.
5.0 Period of Performance The Period of Performance (PoP) for this effort shall be from the date of contract award.180 calendar days
Offerors shall propose the staffing and level of effort they determine necessary to satisfy the SOW within the firm-fixed-price structure and period of performance.
4.0 Place of Performance The place of performance shall be 100% remote at the Vendor's facility.

The architecture must support full data lifecycle management, ensuring that inactive core records (e.g., separated personnel, retired inventory) can be archived and removed from active views, but securely maintained for a specified timeframe to meet audit requirements prior to permanent deletion.

The vendor must facilitate testing cycles, incorporate feedback, and perform any necessary reworks identified by the internal team to guarantee the solution's full operability and alignment with mission requirements.

The vendor will not be provided access to live data, nor will they have on-site access to the Government facility, therefore, a FCL is not required and CUI or classified information will not be provided to the vendor.
For proposal purposes, offerors should assume a single approval level for transactions that affect inventory status, custody, or assignment.
